tasks.short: Watch students during the ride, correct behaviour, and write behaviour notes for the school.

steps.what: Bus monitor monitors the conduct of students during the ride
Bus monitor corrects behaviour to maintain discipline and safety
Bus monitor writes behaviour notes for the school: on paper forms today, on a short phone form with student, time and type after the change
Bus monitor checks the note before it goes: the student, what happened, and the school contact it goes to
Bus monitor submits the checked note to the school contact: by handing the paper form in at the depot today, by submitting it in the app after the change

tasks.design: Behaviour notes are entered on a short form in a phone app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) after the ride, with student, time and type of incident, and the monitor checks each note and its recipient before submitting it to the school's contact, instead of paper forms handed in at the depot. Watching and correcting students stay with the monitor. No cameras analyse students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were written on paper and reached the school days later.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple phone forms route notes to the right school.
tasks.still_hard: Monitors on split shifts write notes late.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which child acts up because something is wrong at home.

reach.learn: Whether notes arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Phone forms can route short notes to a named contact.
Emotion recognition is banned under AI Act article 5; no camera analysis is used.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ride start to behaviour noted; school measures are outside.
Input contract: school contacts kept in the app; fallback is paper.
Watching students, correcting them, writing notes (a first record) and checking them keep their full time. Submitting keeps 25 because the note no longer has to be handed in at the depot.
Notes on minors are kept only as long as the school needs them.
research_questions: Do schools act on notes sooner?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: learning the phone form is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: The behaviour note with student, time and what happened exactly as checked by the monitor in s3c, submitted once to the named contact at that student's school; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many monitors keep handing in paper at the depot (0.8); high: notes are submitted in the app (1.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notice delays or accidents, report them to dispatch by radio or phone, inform parents and school, and write the incident report.

steps.what: Bus monitor notices delays, accidents or traffic situations
Bus monitor reports delays and accidents to dispatchers using mobile two-way radios
Bus monitor phones parents and the school about delays
Bus monitor writes the incident report: on paper today, on a phone form with time and position filled from the GPS after the change

tasks.design: The bus's GPS position and expected arrival show on the dispatch screen and in a parents' app ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so routine delays need no radio call to dispatch and parents look up the bus instead of being phoned. Accidents and incidents are still reported by radio at once. The incident report is a phone form with time and position filled from the GPS. Noticing situations and reporting incidents stay with the monitor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every delay meant radio calls to dispatch and phone calls to parents.
tasks.enabler_now: GPS trackers on buses feed dispatch screens and parent apps.
tasks.still_hard: Some parents do not use the app.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping children calm after a crash while waiting for help.

reach.learn: Whether waiting at the stop falls.

evidence.claim: GPS trackers on buses can feed dispatch screens and parent apps with expected arrival times.
GPS and time stamps monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ride start to the incident reported; accident handling by police is outside.
Input contract: GPS fitted on the bus; fallback is radio and phone.
Parents look at the app in about the time a call took; no added parent time.
Works council consent comes before GPS use.

Noticing situations keeps its full time. s2 keeps 80 because routine delays need no radio call and incidents still do; s3 keeps 40 for parents who do not use the app and for the school; s4 keeps 85 because only time and position fill in.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: phoning parents who do not use the app is kept in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: about half of parents do not use the app and dispatch still asks for most delays by radio (10.7); high: most parents use the app (19.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch for tension between students, separate and calm them, and write the incident report for the school.

steps.what: Bus monitor watches for tension between students
Bus monitor prevents or defuses altercations between students
Bus monitor writes the incident report for the school: on paper today, on the phone form with students involved, what happened and action taken after the change
Bus monitor checks the report before it goes: students involved, what happened, action taken and the school contact it goes to
Bus monitor submits the checked report to the school contact: by handing it in at the depot today, by submitting it in the app after the change

tasks.design: Incident reports are a phone form ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with fixed fields (students involved, what happened, action taken) that the monitor checks and then submits to the school's contact, instead of a paper report handed in at the depot. Watching for tension and defusing altercations stay with the monitor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were written on paper after the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone forms route reports to schools.
tasks.still_hard: Accounts of a fight differ between students.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping between two children before a push becomes a fight.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Phone forms can route incident reports to a named contact.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ride start to the incident reported; school sanctions are outside.
Input contract: school contacts kept in the app; fallback is paper.
Watching, defusing altercations, writing the report (a first record) and checking it keep their full time. Submitting keeps 25 because the report no longer has to be handed in at the depot.
Reports on minors are kept only as long as needed.
research_questions: Do schools respond to incidents sooner?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: learning the incident form is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: The incident report exactly as checked by the monitor in s3c, submitted once to the named contact at the students' school; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many monitors keep handing in paper at the depot (0.8); high: reports are submitted in the app (1.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer students' questions on the bus, pass on requests and complaints to the school or transport office, and note recurring complaints.

steps.what: Bus monitor responds to students' questions and requests on the bus
Bus monitor passes students' complaints on: by phoning the school or transport office today, by writing them on the phone form after the change
Bus monitor checks the complaint before it goes: what the student asked, the type and the office it routes to
Bus monitor submits the checked complaint, which goes to the school or transport office for its type
Bus monitor notes recurring complaints on paper

tasks.design: Requests and complaints are written on a phone form ({OPS_SYSTEM}); the monitor checks the text, type and office, and the form routes them to the school or the transport office by type (route, seating, lost property, behaviour), instead of phoning around. The form keeps a log, so recurring complaints show up without a separate list. Answering students on the bus stays with the monitor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints were passed on by phone and tracked on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone forms route requests by type and keep a log.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent requests still need a call.
tasks.human_edge: Reassuring a young child who is scared of the ride.

evidence.claim: Phone forms can route requests by type and keep a log.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student question to complaints noted; resolving complaints is outside.
Input contract: routing set by the transport office; fallback is phone.

Answering students and checking each complaint keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because writing the complaint takes about half the time phoning around did; s3 keeps 50 because recurring complaints show in the log and noting what they mean stays.

incremental.description: Bus monitor phones about urgent requests as well.

approvals.approved_version: The complaint or request with its type exactly as checked by the monitor in s2c, sent once to the school or transport office that the type routes to; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the offices still want a call for most complaints (8.1); high: the form replaces most calls (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The bus monitor keeps watching, calming and helping students; paper notes, routine radio calls and phone calls to parents shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A monitor with more attention for the children.
